Second day in Vietnam and I find an absolute treasure.
Aug 2026 • Solo
Heard so much about the craft beer culture in Saigon hat I had to try one. August, second day in Vietnam I picked this taproom. Now, my favourite in the whole world is Apocalypse Now and I hadn't put 2 and 2 together to realise this was dedicated to the movie and, of course, Joseph Conrad's "Heart of Darkness" novel.

What a great bar. I tried three different beers and the final one I had three of....... Tghis was Kurtz's Insane IPA. What a beer, what a beautiful beer. At $6.55 AUD for a schooner I glad I pulled out to go back to the hotel when I did or I'd still be there.

Taproom is lovely, unpretentious, well decorated, the food was delicious (of course) and the staff working there were an absolute delight. I bought a T-Shirt and a glass there as well (both Kurtz's Insane IPA). Sooooo, Ill be back here at the end of my journey through Vietnam. 

To add to all the time there I started talking to another Australian guy in the bar. OMG he grew up in Eltham, which is where I grew up and he went to Eltham High School which is where I went. This always happens to me.

Cam on Heart of Darkness Brewery and the incredible team there. See you again soon.

A fantastic craft brewery in the heart of HCMC
Dec 2022 • Business
I started with their lager. Why? Because with a lager there’s nowhere to hide. A decent brewer can make a good ale, but it takes a great brewer to have the consistency required for a lager. 

Heart of Darkness passed that test. The lager had flavour, with a clean finish, and would go down great on any warm day (or a cold one n front of a fire). 

I had the lamb Barbados tacos. I will say that you should expect the tacos to be the smaller street taco version, but what they lack in size their make up for in rich flavour. If you’re looking for something substantial maybe consider the burgers. 

I closed out the night with their limited edition Ghost barrel aged stout. I preface this noting I lived in Belgium for years. I routinely stalk my local liquor stores for the best beer. The Ghost Stout was probably the most flavourful beer I’d had since the Gouden Carolus Cuvée Van De Keizer. The Ghost had a nose strong in black liquorice, with strong tasting notes of wood, peat, and vanilla, together with some candied dark fruits. It’s mouthfeel was thick. It made you want to gulp it down while also being so strong and such a forceful mouthfeel to make you slow down and appreciate it, sip by sip. While I may quibble that it was slightly more barley wine than stout, I cannot argue with it being sublime. 

It’s pricey for Vietnam, but was fantastic. If it was in Canada I’d be a regular.

a quick pint, but just the one!
Sep 2022
Here twice......interesting place.

I like how they got the bar temperature exactly perfect. As you walk into the bar from the heat outside its very refreshing as the bar is well cool and chilled........ That could be me though, who knows! But it was definitely a factor in me returning the second time, knowing how well air-conditioned the premises was. Something that's very important when drinking cold beers! 
Has also good lightning and a cool decor. Its an easy place to sit back and relax. 

The beer menu is quite detailed, a lot to choose from......
I went for the Tropical Bia, Mango and Passion Fruit, the Directors Chocolate Porter and the On the Spot New England IPA. 
The IPA hit the spot, lovely and cold.......the Fruit beer was well tasty, but the Porter wasn't my cup of tea, but that is porter always a hit or miss......but overall the beers were good and full of flavours.

The service first time was spot on, less so the second time. For sure the young girl was busy on her own and very busy with an order up stairs, but I'd say I was waiting a good 20 minutes to get served.......

Also the prices are a bit steep.......very steep for Vietnam..... Nearly nine euros the last outing.... JHC It was like I was back in Switzerland...... 

Worth a venture in for a quick pint, but just the one!

Came for the IPA, stayed for the porter
Dec 2019
I stopped by this brewery for a quick flight. After two weeks of vacation, drinking thin yellow beer (Chang, Singha, Beerlao, Bia Ha Noi, Bia Saigon, Larue....), I was craving something more substantial. 

I ordered a flight of three of their IPAs (Loose Rivet NEIPA, Spirit of Adventure west coast IPA, The Mistress double IPA) plus their Director's cacao nib porter. 

The Spirit of Adventure was fine, the Loose Rivet and Mistress were great, and the Director's porter was surprisingly fantastic. I'm usually not much of a porter guy but this was really damn good. 

I live in New York City and am spoiled having a number of world-class breweries within a few miles of home. I can confidently say that Heart of Darkness would hold its own in any market, not just in HCMC. 

I didn't try the food since I was on my way to dinner, but for what it's worth, the stuff coming out of the kitchen looked and smelled great. 

The ambiance reminded me of a brew pub you might find in the western United States. Stepping off the sidewalk of HCMC you feel like you've walked into a different country. I had mixed feelings about the fact that most patrons there were clearly foreigners/tourists, but on the other hand, you can't "live like a local" while drinking distinctly Western-style beers. 

I can't say for sure, but I'd wager that this is some of the best beer in Southeast Asia. Check it out if you're nearby.
